purpose: Instruction variant for prompt selection: directs attention to the category.
note: Identical to version 1 except for the instruction, so a difference between versions is the wording's. Written for prompt selection on the control development split; it says nothing about how often a name is wrong or how any set was built.
system: You inspect records from a public map database and judge whether the name they carry belongs to them. Answer only with the JSON object the schema describes.
instruction: Compare the name shown with the record's category. Decide whether the name plausibly belongs to an establishment of this kind at this location, or whether it belongs to some other place. Answer with the JSON object alone.

views.name_only: Here is the record's name, and nothing else about it.
views.tags_only: Here is everything the record shows except its name.
views.neither: Here is the record's position, and nothing else about it.

exemplar_intro: Two worked examples follow. They are invented records, not entries from the database.

verdict.description: belongs when the name plausibly belongs to this establishment, wrong when it belongs to some other place
